Chloromethane coordinate fixtures and experimental comparison
===========================================================

Coordinate provenance
The accompanying JSON retains unscaled, unrounded coordinates and atom order
from Zenodo record 18232165, data.zip, data/nmrshiftdb2/All/valid.lmdb:
https://zenodo.org/api/records/18232165/files/data.zip/content
CH3Cl: ASCII key 2213 (hex 32323133).
CH2Cl2: ASCII key 112 (hex 313132).
Archive, member, and serialized-record SHA256 values are retained in the JSON.
The records were decoded in a contained, offline scan after archive/member
verification. Only atoms and coordinates were selected; no labels are needed.
Names and carbon-to-each-other-atom single bonds are assigned here; the source
records have no molecule name or bond graph.

Experimental reference provenance (accessed 2026-10-17)
NIST Computational Chemistry Comparison and Benchmark Database (CCCBDB),
Standard Reference Database 101, release 22 (May 2022), experimental geometry,
"Internal coordinates" table; distances explicitly in angstroms:

* CH3Cl, methyl chloride / chloromethane, CAS 74-87-3, neutral:
  https://cccbdb.nist.gov/expgeom2x.asp?casno=74873&charge=0
  rCH = 1.090 Å; rCCl = 1.785 Å.
  NIST reference identifier: 1973Dun/McK:232.
  The table does not specify a structure convention in its comment column.

* CH2Cl2, methylene chloride / dichloromethane, CAS 75-09-2, neutral:
  https://cccbdb.nist.gov/expgeom2x.asp?casno=75092&charge=0
  rCH = 1.085 Å; rCCl = 1.767 Å.
  NIST reference identifier: 1998Kuc.
  Both entries are marked rs (substitution structure), not equilibrium re.

Use the tabulated internal-coordinate values, rather than distances recomputed
from NIST's rounded Cartesian display. NIST is the consulted source; the cited
underlying publications have not been independently inspected.

Test meaning and tolerance
tests/test_bond_distances.py compares every proposed bond directly with these
experimental values, interpreting one stored coordinate unit as one angstrom.
Absolute tolerances are 0.01 Å for C-H and 0.04 Å for C-Cl. These are local
geometry acceptance thresholds, not NIST error bars or measurement precision.
The C-Cl allowance deliberately accommodates the observed roughly 0.018 Å
(CH3Cl) and 0.036 Å (CH2Cl2) discrepancies; 0.01 Å would fail those bonds.
This is a coarse physical-scale check and would reject a factor-of-ten unit
error. It does not demonstrate experimental accuracy or reproduce the small
experimental C-Cl contraction: both released geometries have C-Cl near 1.803.
It checks two retained records, not all model inputs or the training pipeline,
and does not change inference unit admission.
